newsitem.title: USA: Pontiac-GMC sees 1.2 mln units '97 U.S sales.
newsitem.headline: Pontiac-GMC sees 1.2 mln units '97 U.S sales.

text.p: The head of General Motors Corp's Pontiac-GMC division said Monday he expects the division to sell 1.2 million automobiles in the United States in 1997, up from about 1.1 million last year.

Roy Roberts, general manager of the division which was formed when the Pontiac and GMC division were combined last year, said he expected the GMC part of the division to account for 500,000 of the sales, with Pontiac accounting for the rest.
Roberts said the merger of the two brands was completed in eight months, much sooner than the 1-3/4 to two years originally forecast.

Roberts also said the division was considering developing a truck-car hybrid automobile and said questions about whether that auto would be developed might be answered at the Pontiac presentation Tuesday at the North American International Auto Show.
"We think there's something going on in that area," Roberts said of consumer demand for the hybrid.
On Monday, Pontiac-GMC unveiled the Yukon Denali, an upscale version of the popular sport utility vehicle.
Roberts would not comment specifically on pricing, but said the vehicle was slated to be in production in the 1998 calendar year.
The vehicle includes four heated seats and a 255 horse power, 5.7 liter engine, GM said.
